title: Enable [landing] merge_via_rest in athena.toml
summary: Add a [landing] table to athena.toml with merge_via_rest = true and a comment giving the reason (squash-only repo, ruleset on main, owner approved merging verified work once required checks pass). Nothing else changes.

defaults_applied.how: Comment contains no secrets or personal data.
Comment explains the reason for an outside reader.
The setting is enforced by code in gh.rs, which reads it.

assumptions: athena.toml has no existing [landing] table (grep found none), so one is added, placed after existing tables or near related config.
The setting is read as config.landing.merge_via_rest (crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs) and defaults to off when absent.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml contains a [landing] table with merge_via_rest = true, appearing exactly once.

A comment directly above the setting states the reason: the repository is squash-only with a ruleset on main (required checks, linear history, no force push), and the owner approved merging verified work once required checks pass.
No other line of athena.toml changes, and no other file changes.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo check`; the config still parses and tests pass. `git diff` shows only the added [landing] lines in athena.toml.

out_of_scope: Changing code, docs, CHANGELOG, or CI workflows
Changing repository settings or the GitHub ruleset
departures: Tiny single-file config change, so cheaper, faster, and likelier to pass than the reference.
